::: {.callout-note role="note" aria-label="Note" markdown="1"}
**Update (25 November 2026)**

This post now uses **ggplot2**.
:::

Sometimes you want to produce maps with special layouts. I especially like maps
with modified geometries, e.g. simplifying the original shapes to squares or
dots. When searching the web, I found the fantastic post [Fishnets and
Honeycomb: Square vs. Hexagonal Spatial
Grids](https://strimas.com/post/hexagonal-grids/) by [Matt
Strimas-Mackey](https://strimas.com/#about), which was a huge inspiration (by
the way, don't miss [his blog](http://strimas.com/#posts), full of very
interesting pieces of work).

The only thing I was not completely comfortable with was that the post used the
[old-fashioned](https://r.geocompx.org/) **sp** package instead of my personal
favorite, the **sf** package. The post was published in 2016, and note that the
author has also moved to the **sf** package since then. So I decided to explore
further options with **sf**.

The approach is similar, using grids over a map and working with them, but with
[st_make_grid()](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/reference/st_make_grid.html).
I also expanded it by grouping the grids and producing dots over the geometries.
So basically I produced five variations of the map:

| Type          | Replacement | Grouped |
|---------------|:-----------:|:-------:|
| **Fishnet**   |   Square    |   No    |
| **Puzzle**    |   Square    |   Yes   |
| **Honeycomb** |   Hexagon   |   No    |
| **Hexbin**    |   Hexagon   |   Yes   |
| **Pixel**     |     Dot     |   No    |

## Required **R** packages

```{r}
#| label: libs

library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)


# Define a common theme for the maps.
background <- "#FAF8F2"
foreground <- "#203B47"
map_title <- "inter-tight"
map_regular <- "inter"

sysfonts::font_add_google("Inter Tight", family = map_title)
sysfonts::font_add_google("Inter", family = map_regular)
showtext::showtext_opts(dpi = knitr::opts_chunk$get("dpi"))
showtext::showtext_auto()

theme_set(
  theme_void(paper = background, base_family = map_regular, ink = foreground) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(family = map_title, face = "bold"),
      legend.title = element_text(family = map_title, face = "bold"),
      strip.text = element_text(family = map_title, face = "bold"),
      plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
    )
)
```

## Working with square grids

Let's use the `square` option of `st_make_grid()` and play a bit with it.

```{r}
#| label: 20190602_preparing
#| fig-cap: ""
uk <- rnaturalearth::ne_download(50,
  type = "map_subunits",
  returnclass = "sf",
  destdir = tempdir()
) %>%
  filter(CONTINENT == "Europe") %>%
  filter(ADM0_A3 == "GBR") %>%
  # Projecting and cleaning
  st_transform(3857) %>%
  select(NAME_EN, ADM0_A3)

initial <- uk %>%
  # Iteration using indexes
  mutate(index_target = row_number())
```

::: {.callout-caution role="note" aria-label="Caution" markdown="1"}
The `cellsize` should be set in the same unit as the projection (in this case,
meters). Pay special attention to this because if the parameter is too small,
meaning that the grid is too dense, **R** could crash easily.
:::

```{r}
#| label: 20190602_squares
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Two maps of United Kingdom comparing separate square grid cells with cells
#|   merged into regional shapes. Colors distinguish regions.

# Grid to sf
grid <- initial %>%
  st_make_grid(50 * 1000,
    # Kms
    crs = st_crs(initial),
    what = "polygons",
    square = TRUE
  ) %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  mutate(index = row_number())

# We identify the grids that belong to an entity by assessing the centroid
cent_merge <- grid %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  st_filter(initial) %>%
  st_join(initial)

grid_new <- grid %>% inner_join(st_drop_geometry(cent_merge))

# Fishnet
fish_geom <- grid_new %>%
  group_by(NAME_EN) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), do_union = FALSE)


# Now let's create the puzzle
puzzle_geom <- grid_new %>%
  # Avoid slivers
  st_buffer(0.5) %>%
  group_by(NAME_EN) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), do_union = TRUE) # The only difference is do_union

# Plot

fish_geom %>%
  mutate(label = "Fishnet") %>%
  bind_rows(
    puzzle_geom %>%
      mutate(label = "Puzzle")
  ) %>%
  mutate(label = forcats::fct_inorder(label)) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = NAME_EN), show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~label) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo")
```

## Going hex

Extremely easy. We just need to change the `square` parameter of
`st_make_grid()` from `TRUE` to `FALSE`.

```{r}
#| label: 20190602_hex
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Two maps of United Kingdom comparing separate hexagonal grid cells with
#|   cells merged into regional shapes. Colors distinguish regions.

# Grid to sf
grid_hex <- initial %>%
  st_make_grid(50 * 1000,
    # Kms
    crs = st_crs(initial),
    what = "polygons",
    square = FALSE # This is the only piece that changes!!!
  ) %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  mutate(index = row_number())

cent_merge_hex <- grid_hex %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  st_filter(initial) %>%
  st_join(initial)

grid_hex_new <- grid_hex %>% inner_join(st_drop_geometry(cent_merge_hex))

# Honeycomb
honey_geom <- grid_hex_new %>%
  group_by(NAME_EN) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), do_union = FALSE)


# Now let's create the hexbin
hexbin_geom <- grid_hex_new %>%
  # Avoid slivers
  st_buffer(0.5) %>%
  group_by(NAME_EN) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), do_union = TRUE) # The only difference is do_union

# Plot

honey_geom %>%
  mutate(label = "Honeycomb") %>%
  bind_rows(
    hexbin_geom %>%
      mutate(label = "Hexbin")
  ) %>%
  mutate(label = forcats::fct_inorder(label)) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = NAME_EN), show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~label) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo")
```

## Pixel it!

Also quite easy, just a couple more tweaks, still using `st_make_grid()`.

```{r}
#| label: 20190602_pix
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Map of Great Britain represented by separated square pixels, colored by
#|   region.

grid_pixels <- initial %>%
  st_make_grid(50 * 1000,
    # Kms
    crs = st_crs(initial),
    what = "centers",
    square = TRUE
  ) %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  mutate(index = row_number())

pixels_geom <- grid_pixels %>%
  st_filter(initial) %>%
  # We need to buffer the points to get polygons, based on the grid resolution
  st_buffer(50 * 1000 / 2) %>%
  st_join(initial) %>%
  group_by(NAME_EN) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), do_union = FALSE)


# Plot
ggplot(pixels_geom) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = NAME_EN), show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  labs(title = "Pixel")
```

## Wrap up

Finally, I wrapped all that in a function named `stdh_gridpol()`. See the code
in [my
repo](https://github.com/dieghernan/dieghernan.github.io/tree/master/assets/functions):

```{r}
#| label: 20190602_function
stdh_gridpol <- function(sf,
                         to = "fishnet",
                         gridsize = as.integer(
                           min(
                             diff(st_bbox(sf)[c(1, 3)]),
                             diff(st_bbox(sf)[c(2, 4)])
                           ) / 40
                         ),
                         sliver = 0.5) {
  if (!unique(st_geometry_type(sf)) %in% c("POLYGON", "MULTIPOLYGON")) {
    stop("Input should be MULTIPOLYGON or POLYGON")
  }
  if (!to %in% c("fishnet", "puzzle", "honeycomb", "hexbin", "pixel")) {
    stop("'to' should be 'fishnet','puzzle','honeycomb','hexbin' or 'pixel'")
  }

  if (class(sf)[1] == "sf") {
    initial <- sf
    initial$index_target <- 1:nrow(initial)
  } else {
    initial <- st_sf(index_target = 1:length(sf), geom = sf)
  }

  target <- st_geometry(initial)

  if (to %in% c("fishnet", "puzzle")) {
    sq <- T
  } else {
    sq <- F
  }
  if (to == "pixel") {
    grid <- st_make_grid(target,
      gridsize,
      crs = st_crs(initial),
      what = "centers"
    )
  } else {
    grid <- st_make_grid(
      target,
      gridsize,
      crs = st_crs(initial),
      what = "polygons",
      square = sq
    )
  }
  grid <- st_sf(index = 1:length(lengths(grid)), grid) # Add index
  if (to == "pixel") {
    cent_merge <- st_join(grid, initial["index_target"], left = F)
    grid_new <- st_buffer(cent_merge, gridsize / 2)
  } else {
    cent_grid <- st_centroid(grid)
    cent_merge <- st_join(cent_grid, initial["index_target"], left = F)
    grid_new <- inner_join(grid, st_drop_geometry(cent_merge))
  }
  if (to %in% c("fishnet", "honeycomb", "pixel")) {
    geom <- aggregate(
      grid_new,
      by = list(grid_new$index_target),
      FUN = min,
      do_union = FALSE
    )
  } else {
    geom <- aggregate(
      st_buffer(grid_new, sliver),
      by = list(grid_new$index_target),
      FUN = min,
      do_union = TRUE
    )
  }
  if (class(initial)[1] == "sf") {
    fin <- left_join(
      geom %>% select(index_target),
      st_drop_geometry(initial)
    ) %>%
      select(-index_target)
    fin <- st_cast(fin, "MULTIPOLYGON")
    return(fin)
  } else {
    fin <- st_cast(geom, "MULTIPOLYGON")
    return(st_geometry(fin))
  }
}
# End of the function-----

fish <- stdh_gridpol(uk, to = "fishnet", gridsize = 50 * 1000)
puzz <- stdh_gridpol(uk, to = "puzzle", gridsize = 50 * 1000)
hon <- stdh_gridpol(uk, to = "honeycomb", gridsize = 50 * 1000)
hex <- stdh_gridpol(uk, to = "hexbin", gridsize = 50 * 1000)
pix <- stdh_gridpol(uk, to = "pixel", gridsize = 50 * 1000)
```

```{r}
#| label: 20190602_functionex
#| fig-height: 7.75
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-dpi: 300
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Six maps of the United Kingdom compare the original boundaries with square
#|   cells, merged squares, hexagonal cells, merged hexagons and dots.

grid_maps <- bind_rows(
  list(
    Original = uk,
    Fishnet = fish,
    Puzzle = puzz,
    Honeycomb = hon,
    Hexbin = hex,
    Pixel = pix
  ),
  .id = "method"
) |>
  mutate(
    method = factor(
      method,
      levels = c("Original", "Fishnet", "Puzzle", "Honeycomb", "Hexbin", "Pixel")
    )
  )

ggplot(grid_maps) +
  geom_sf(
    aes(fill = NAME_EN),
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  facet_wrap(vars(method), nrow = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Redrawing the United Kingdom",
    subtitle = "Original boundaries and five representations on a 50 km grid"
  )
```

And that's it! The function `stdh_gridpol()` has some alert mechanisms, such as
accepting only `POLYGON` or `MULTIPOLYGON`, and the default value of `gridsize`
is computed so that the shortest dimension has 40 cells.

```{r}
#| label: 20190602_imgpost
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| fig-height: 5.3
#| fig-width: 8
world <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(returnclass = "sf")
world <- st_transform(world, "+proj=robin")
world2 <- stdh_gridpol(world, "pixel", gridsize = 300000)


ggplot(world2) +
  geom_sf(fill = "#1fc2ff", color = "#505050") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#505050"),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )
```
